about: The work packaging/experience_run.py plays in every scenario. briefs: the corpus; an entry is either {case: <id in references/classifier-cases.json>} (its task text and expected_profile) or {text, profile} written here with the profile a classifier would give (all task-profile fields). split_into: the briefs a session writes when roll answers split. day: one working day, in order; at is the hour of the day. Each entry is a roll of one brief, or of several (briefs) in one roll; label names the worker it launches, resume rolls a follow-up to that worker (--resume); can_wait_hours passes --can-wait-hours; named is a route the user named (family, model, effort, basis; the scenario's first account of that family is named, or the family's name when it has none); workspace passes --workspace <work dir>/<name>; worker is how the fixture worker ends (ok | error | crash | slow | quota); fault is the Paseo host fixture's fault for the next create (reject | uncertain). error_scopes: the scope the fixture classifier answers when the router asks it to read a worker's error (provider_retry's scope question), for each error text a fixture worker or the fixture host writes (packaging/zero_fake_cli.py, packaging/zero_fake_paseo_bridge.mjs): what a classifier reading that text would say; a text not listed gets no answer (unknown).

fixture worker failure.why: the worker says its task could not be completed: its own work failed, not the provider

You've hit your usage limit. Try again l.why: the provider's usage-limit refusal of the signed-in account

Free usage limit reached. Connect a prov.why: OpenCode's free-limit refusal (provider.free-limit, 429) of the signed-in account's free allowance

worker process vanished.why: the host saw the worker's process end without a word: nothing in the text says whose doing it was

two_webgpu.text: Survey the public WebGPU browser support tables for Safari, Chrome and Firefox (desktop and mobile) and return a short table with the version each first shipped it and any flag still needed.

two_flag_audit.text: Audit git diff v0.4.3..HEAD in D:/work/app for command-line flags that were renamed, removed or changed meaning; list each with the commit and whether a user script would break.

three_translate.text: Translate docs/faq.md of this checkout into natural Japanese, keeping code spans, links and headings unchanged; write docs/faq.ja.md.

three_benchmark.text: Benchmark SQLite WAL checkpoint latency with the scripts in scripts/ at 1, 10 and 100 MB of WAL; report the median and p95 of each and the command lines used.

three_icons.text: Design three distinct app icon concepts as standalone SVG files (a compass motif, flat style, legible at 16 px); return the SVG text of each.

many_pricing.text: Research the public pricing pages of three competing task-router products and return their plan names, prices and limits with links.

many_backstories.text: Write five short character backstories (150 words each) for the cast of a cozy mystery game set in a mountain library; each with a secret and a habit.

many_onboard_audit.text: Review setup/onboard.py in this checkout for error paths that leave a half-written config; list each with the line and a suggested fix, change nothing.

many_screens.text: Classify the 50 UI screenshots in var/screens/ by screen type (login, settings, list, detail, error) into var/screens/labels.csv.

many_tray_icon.text: Fix tray/app.pyw so the tray icon appears at startup when the icon cache is empty; add a test for that case.

module_followup.text: Follow-up to the reservoir sampling module you just wrote: add property-based tests for the weighted case and a short docstring example; keep the public function unchanged.

named_review.text: Review the retry and backoff design written up inline below for failure modes under clock skew and partial network partitions; answer with the three most serious problems. (Design: each client retries with jittered exponential backoff capped at 30 s and a server-side token bucket per tenant.)

named_free_todo.text: List every TODO comment under src/ of this checkout with its file, line and a one-line gist; change nothing.

trivial_typo.text: Fix the typo 'recieve' to 'receive' in README.md of this checkout; touch nothing else.

trivial_rename.text: Rename the local variable tmp to buffer in src/io/reader.py function read_block; run nothing else.

trivial_lookup.text: From the inlined changelog below, list the version numbers that mention 'cache' in one line each. (Changelog: 1.2 cache size option; 1.3 faster startup; 1.4 cache eviction fix; 1.5 new icons.)

workspace_writer_a.text: In this checkout, split src/report/render.py into render_table.py and render_chart.py with no behaviour change; update the imports and run the module's tests.

workspace_writer_b.text: In this checkout, add a --since option to the export command in src/cli/export.py that filters rows by date, with tests.

frontier_proof.text: Prove or refute: the lease-handoff protocol described inline admits no execution where two holders both believe they own the lease, under asynchronous message delivery with crash-recovery. Give a TLA+-style invariant and either a proof sketch or a minimal counterexample trace. (Protocol: holder renews every T/3; a successor may acquire after observing T of silence; clocks drift at most 1%.)
